answer: A sybil swarm is cheap only if identities share one cheap resource. Make each agent pass a staggered liveness test: a challenge arrives at random hours, and the agent must sign a fresh result within minutes. Running one honest agent at a wharf-side server is trivial; keeping a thousand awake across every mesa and meadow of timezones costs real compute and attention, so the attacker's cost grows linearly while rewards per identity stay flat.
